caveats: The publication-disabled simulated-Actions build-core run and the independent native-local build-core run reproduced the stella2014_libretro.zip package, resolver metadata, both ABI artifacts, and both active-marker build logs byte for byte. Execution was local; both builds cloned the pinned source over the network, so no offline source cache is proven.

This is static build/package evidence only. ARM64 is build-identity-bound to ra64-universal-v1 and ARMHF to ra32-a30-v1. ARMHF requires GLIBCXX_3.4.32, above the observed non-enforcing Miyoo Mini fallback provider value GLIBCXX_3.4.24, so the Mini profile is ineligible; A30 is the eligible 32-bit consumer at the ABI screen. Provider inspection and target-runtime capture are absent, so every execution profile and device view remains provisional and ineligible pending a runtime smoke result.

Content, BIOS/firmware handling, controls, audio/video pacing, saves and state round trips, reset and unload behavior, frontend integration, compatibility, licensing review, and sustained performance remain target-runtime and human gates. Publication remains disabled regardless of local byte reproducibility.

The publication-disabled simulated-Actions build-core run and the independent local-profile build-core run reproduced both ABI artifacts, metadata, and the package byte for byte; both runs satisfied the exact mixed-language compile and link proof.

The build command scopes exact native leading-space version ' 4a7da82' through GIT_VERSION; the fail-closed proof binds 14 C and 84 C++ compiles per ABI, exact output/source/argv sets, and the final link-object set. Both ABI logs are warning-free.
The resolver info advertises a26|bin content while the runtime also advertises mvc, so extension and content integration remain target-runtime gates rather than build-time metadata rewrites.
Stella 2014 is GPLv2; any public distribution or release remains a human legal/policy and corresponding-source gate even though the local build is reproducible.

Atari 2600 content loading, MVC behavior, controls, audio/video pacing, saves, states, and sustained performance remain target-runtime gates; static build evidence does not establish device eligibility.

ARM64 requires GLIBC_2.17 and is bound to ra64-universal-v1; ARMHF reaches GLIBCXX_3.4.32 and is bound only to ra32-a30-v1. That C++ floor exceeds the Mini-family observed GLIBCXX_3.4.24 fallback, so no ra32-universal-v0 or Mini eligibility is claimed.
